instrument: ICAO MID PBN SG/8 WP11 (UAE) GNSS anomalies
requirement_paraphrase: UAE reports GPS jamming affecting aircraft in the Emirates FIR (example 3 Oct 2023) and proposes updating state rules to require prompt action and mandatory reporting of interference, with ANSP reporting procedures.

UAE paper A41-WP/196 asks ICAO to bring the operational impact of GNSS interference to States' attention and urges States to implement the mitigation measures in Doc 9849; the three-step process (monitor, assess, mitigate) is described in the body, not named in the requested actions.

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/14 WP05 (UAE) protecting surveillance data integrity against GNSS interference
edition_or_version: Dated 10 Oct 2025; meeting Abu Dhabi 19-23 Oct 2025
requirement_paraphrase: UAE reports an increase in interference cases and suspected spoofing over two years; asks the meeting to encourage MID States to set up surveillance-integrity investigation frameworks and designate national focal points for GNSS interference reporting, and to ask the ICAO MID Office to maintain a regional repository of reports.

instrument: ICAO MID CNS SG/15 WP08 (Saudi Arabia) national GNSS monitoring
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes a national GNSS signal monitoring and reporting system for the Jeddah FIR and a regional RFI database.

status_note: Published; stage 90.92 'to be revised' (2021-07-23), confirmed 2020; ISO/FDIS 13482 under development
requirement_paraphrase: Safety requirements for personal care robots (mobile servant, physical assistant, person carrier): safe design, protective measures, user information. Voluntary standard; not shown as legally binding.
At publication, ISO 13482 noted no exhaustive internationally recognised data such as pain or injury limits existed for collision hazards with personal care robots. Voluntary standard.
applies_to: Personal care robots with physical contact

status_note: Published; stage 90.92 'to be revised' (2025-06-26); to be replaced by ISO/AWI 15066-1
requirement_paraphrase: Technical specification for collaborative industrial robot systems and their work environment, supplementing collaborative guidance in ISO 10218-1/-2; not applicable to collaborative applications designed before its publication.

Methodology for design and integration of safety-related control parts, incl. software, for high-demand/continuous modes; does not define specific safety functions or required performance levels; excludes cybersecurity.
Safety requirements for industrial robot applications and cells across design, integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance, decommissioning and disposal, plus information needed at each stage.
applies_to: Integrators and users of robot cells

requirement_paraphrase: Scope text: applies to functions needing situational awareness from complex sensors and processing algorithms; excludes faults covered by ISO 26262, cybersecurity, and well-proven functions such as airbags.
applies_to: Road vehicles only; excludes mopeds. Interpretation: concepts (functional insufficiency, triggering conditions) may transfer to robots but the standard does not claim scope over them

requirement_paraphrase: Catalogue scope: characteristics, risks, methods and processes for using AI in safety-related work: AI inside a safety function, non-AI safety functions protecting AI-controlled equipment, and AI used as a design tool.
applies_to: Any safety-related system using AI (generic; includes robots)

status_note: Published; ISO page shows stage 90.92 (2025-12-01), ISO/WD TS 5083 in development
requirement_paraphrase: Catalogue scope: guidance on achieving and demonstrating safety of level 3 and 4 automated driving systems: safety by design, V&V, post-deployment activities, cybersecurity outline.
applies_to: Road vehicles incl. trucks and buses; excludes motorcycles and mopeds

requirement_paraphrase: Catalogue scope: safety-related E/E systems using AI in series-production road vehicles, covering vehicle-level risks from AI output insufficiencies, systematic errors and random hardware errors; focus mainly on machine learning.

status_note: Published 2023-06; stage 90.92 'to be revised', ISO/DIS 3691-4 expected; 2020 edition withdrawn
requirement_paraphrase: Safety requirements and verification for driverless industrial trucks, AGVs and AMRs: control system, guidance, automatic/manual/maintenance modes. Annex A covers operating-zone preparation; Annex B lists significant hazards. Excludes public zones (see ISO 13482), roads, explosive atmospheres and severe conditions.
applies_to: Driverless trucks, AGVs, AMRs in industrial settings

instrument: ISO/IEC TS 22440 (Functional safety and AI systems)
status_note: Under development: stage 30.60 close of comment period 2026-04-11 for both; Part 1 project registered 2024-05-06
requirement_paraphrase: Part 1 'Requirements' is a committee draft (ISO/IEC CD TS 22440-1) at stage 30.60, comment period closed 2026-04-11, registered 2026-02-09; the page gives no Part 3 information.
applies_to: AI systems in functional safety (when published)

status_note: In force; Annex III 1.2.1 text not retrieved
requirement_paraphrase: Secondary source says safety functions and settings must not be easily modifiable beyond the manufacturer's risk analysis limits, including by ML adjustment, and that safety decision data of self-learning machines is kept at least one year; the five year tracing log was not seen.
applies_to: Machinery with control systems, incl. self-learning
